title: On the Phone
description: Learn to make and answer phone calls
objectives: Ask to speak to someone (Can I speak to...? / Is... there?)
Take and leave messages (Can I take a message?)
End phone calls politely (Talk to you later / Goodbye)

phrases: Who is calling? / Who is this?
target_language.grammar_pattern:
This is + name (introducing yourself)
Can I speak to + name?
Is + name + there?

Examples:
- Hello, this is Ahmed
- Can I speak to Marcus?
- Is Marcus there?
- Hold on, please

grammar_patterns.label: Phone introduction
examples: Good morning, this is Ahmed Hassan

grammar_patterns.label: Asking to speak to someone
examples: Can I speak to Dr. Smith?
Can I speak to the manager?

story.context: You call Marcus on the phone. His roommate answers.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi. This is Ahmed. Is Marcus there?

dialogue.speaker: Roommate
dialogue.text: Hold on, please. I'll get him.

dialogue.speaker: Roommate
dialogue.text: Sorry, he's not here right now. Can I take a message?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, please. Can you tell him Ahmed called?

dialogue.speaker: Roommate
dialogue.text: Sure. Ahmed. Does he have your number?

dialogue.speaker: Roommate
dialogue.text: Okay. I'll tell him you called.

drills.title: Drill 1: Introducing yourself on the phone
drills.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word
drills.your_turn: Now introduce yourself on the phone, out loud, and record it

drills.title: Drill 2: Asking to speak to someone
drills.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct name or word
examples: Can I speak to the manager?
drills.your_turn: Now ask to speak to someone you know, out loud, and record it

drills.title: Drill 3: Taking messages
drills.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word

prompts.sentence: Would you like to ___ a message?
Do you want him to call you ___?

examples: Would you like to leave a message?
Can I tell him you called?
Do you want him to call you back?
drills.your_turn: Now offer to take a message for someone, out loud, and record it

listening.question: Listen: Who is calling?
listening.transcript: Hello. This is Ahmed. Can I speak to Marcus?

listening.question: Listen: Is Marcus there?
listening.transcript: Is Marcus there? No, he's not here right now.
listening.explanation: The person says 'He's not here right now'

listening.question: Listen: What does the caller want?
listening.transcript: Would you like to leave a message? Yes, I would like to leave a message.
listening.explanation: The caller wants to leave a message

speaking.title: Task 1: Answer the phone
speaking.instruction: Record yourself answering the phone and introducing yourself.

speaking.title: Task 2: Leave a message
speaking.instruction: Record yourself calling someone who isn't there. Leave a message asking them to call you back.
speaking.example: Hi, this is Ahmed. Is Marcus there? ... Okay. Can you tell him Ahmed called? Please ask him to call me back. Thank you.

writing.title: Task 1: Write a phone message
writing.instruction: Write a phone message. Include: who called, who they want to talk to, and what they want.
writing.example:
Message for: Marcus
From: Ahmed
Message: Please call him back.
Phone: (555) 123-4567

writing.title: Task 2: Write a phone conversation
writing.instruction: Write a conversation (10-12 lines) where you call someone's house and they're not home. Leave a message.
writing.example:
Person: Hello?
You: Hi. This is Ahmed. Is Marcus there?
Person: No, he's not here. Can I take a message?
You: Yes, please. Can you tell him Ahmed called?
Person: Sure. Does he have your number?
You: Yes, he has it.
Person: Okay. I'll tell him.
You: Thank you!
Person: No problem. Goodbye.
You: Goodbye.

sections.title: This is vs I am on the phone
examples: On phone: I am Ahmed (sounds strange)
sections.question: What do we say on the phone?
sections.explanation: On the phone, we say 'This is [name]' not 'I am [name]'. This is a special phone rule in English.

sections.title: Is [person] there? vs Can I speak to [person]?
examples: Is Marcus there? (asking if he's home/available)
Can I speak to Marcus? (asking to talk to him)
sections.question: What's the difference?
sections.explanation: Both questions are asking if you can talk to someone. 'Is [person] there?' is slightly more casual. Both are polite and common.

sections.title: Hold on vs Wait
sections.question: What do these mean?
sections.explanation: These all mean 'wait a short time'. 'Hold on' and 'One moment' are very common on the phone. They're all polite ways to ask someone to wait.

quiz.question: You call someone. How do you introduce yourself on the phone?
quiz.explanation: On the phone, we say 'This is Ahmed' to introduce ourselves.

quiz.question: You want to talk to Marcus. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: 'Is Marcus there?' or 'Can I speak to Marcus?' are polite ways to ask.

quiz.question: Someone calls for Marcus, but he's not home. You say:
options: He's not here. Can I take a message?
quiz.explanation: 'He's not here. Can I take a message?' is helpful and polite.

quiz.question: Someone is looking for Marcus. You need to check. You say:
quiz.explanation: 'Hold on, please' or 'One moment' are polite ways to ask someone to wait.

quiz.question: You want to leave a message. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: 'Can I leave a message?' is the polite way to ask.

quiz.question: Someone answers the phone 'Hello?' What do you say first?
options: Hello, this is Ahmed. Is Marcus there?
quiz.explanation: Say who you are first, then ask for the person. 'Hello, this is Ahmed. Is Marcus there?' is polite and clear.

quiz.question: You answer the phone at work. Someone asks for your boss. Your boss is in a meeting. You say:
options: He's not here right now. Can I take a message?
quiz.explanation: 'He's not here right now' or 'He's not available' + 'Can I take a message?' is professional and helpful.

quiz.question: Which is the MOST polite?
options: Can I speak to Marcus, please?
quiz.explanation: 'Can I speak to Marcus, please?' is the most polite because it uses 'Can I' and 'please'.

quiz.question: Write a 6-line phone conversation where you call Dr. Smith's office and she's not available. Leave a message.
quiz.explanation: Your conversation should include: introducing yourself, asking for Dr. Smith, being told she's not available, and leaving a message.

quiz.question: Think about a real phone call you need to make. Who will you call? What will you say? Write 2-3 sentences.
quiz.explanation: Practice with a real situation from your life. This helps you prepare for actual phone calls.
